reason: Reviewed-equivalent: params are a JS object, so its keys are unique strings; the strict encoder (enc) is injective on every string it can encode and voids the whole base string on any it cannot (tested: two keys that cannot be encoded give an empty base string, never one collapsed empty key), so the encoded keys are unique too. For distinct a and b, a<b and a<=b decide identically, and the equal-key case the flip would change can never occur. The OAuth vector test pins the resulting order on real data.
